Restore the edges removed by pruning

Source: R/deprune_htna.R
deprune_htna.Rd

deprune_htna() restores the edges that prune_htna() removed: it returns the network with every removed edge put back at its original weight. Pruning sets weak edges aside rather than deleting them, so restoring them gives back the full network, for example to compare the pruned and the unpruned structure or to apply a different rule.

deprune_htna() runs Nestimate's net_deprune() with the actor partition kept. The rule stays recorded, so reprune_htna() can apply it again.

Usage

deprune_htna(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network pruned with prune_htna().

...

Unused.

Value

An htna network with the original weight matrix.

See also

prune_htna(), reprune_htna(), pruning_details_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
pruned <- prune_htna(net, threshold = 0.05)
deprune_htna(pruned)
